11.9.    EXEC-009 Material Execution Deviation

Where an actual or intended implementation materially differs from the authorised Pricing
Proposal version or authorised decision baseline, the system must not treat that deviation as
authorised by the existing approval or policy authorisation.

Where the material deviation is identified before implementation, the system must require
either:

    ● correction of the intended implementation so that it matches the authorised decision
          baseline; or
    ● progression of the materially changed pricing action through the applicable Pricing
          Proposal and organisational decision process before implementation.

Where a material deviation is identified after implementation has occurred, the system must:

    ● preserve the actual implemented pricing state;
    ● identify the affected scope;
    ● preserve the implementation timestamp and responsible user;
    ● record the deviation as an Implementation Exception;
    ● preserve the difference between the authorised and implemented action;
    ● require appropriate remediation, follow-up pricing work or organisational decision
          treatment according to applicable policy.

An approval or policy authorisation attached to the original Pricing Proposal version must not
be retrospectively extended or reinterpreted to authorise a materially different implemented
action.

The execution layer must not independently authorise a material deviation.

title: Execution Status and Partial Implementation
requirement:
11.10.       EXEC-010 Execution Status and Partial Implementation

The MVP must maintain execution status separately from Pricing Proposal status and
Pricing Initiative lifecycle state.

Supported execution statuses must include:

    ● Not Started;
    ● In Progress;
    ● Partially Implemented;
    ● Implemented;
    ● Implementation Exception.

Not Started indicates that implementation of the authorised pricing action has not begun.

In Progress indicates that implementation has begun but has not yet reached a completed
implementation state.

Partially Implemented indicates that only part of the authorised pricing scope has been
implemented.

Implemented indicates that the applicable authorised pricing action has been implemented
across the required execution scope, subject to any separately recorded variance.

Implementation Exception indicates that implementation cannot validly continue or be
represented as normally completed because of a material deviation, blocking condition,
failed implementation or other consequential execution issue.

For pricing actions affecting multiple priceable entities, locations, channels or other pricing
dimensions, the system must preserve enough component-level execution information to
identify what has and has not been implemented.

Aggregate execution status must not conceal incomplete, failed or materially divergent
implementation.

Execution status must not modify the Pricing Proposal's Approved or Authorised Within
Policy status.

title: Current Price Update
requirement:
11.14.       EXEC-014 Current Price Update

Where implementation is confirmed and the applicable organisation pricing record is
maintained inside Owómidé, the system should allow the actual implemented selling price to
establish or update the applicable Price Record.

The resulting Price Record must identify, where applicable:

   ● affected Priceable Entity;
   ● actual implemented price;
   ● currency;
   ● applicable pricing dimensions;
   ● actual effective date or timestamp;
   ● originating Pricing Initiative;
   ● authorised Pricing Proposal version;
   ● Execution Record;
   ● implementing or confirming user;

   ● source and provenance.

Where the implemented price becomes presently applicable to that exact pricing context, the
resulting Price Record should become the Current Price in accordance with DATA-003.

Establishing the implemented price as Current Price must not overwrite the Price Record
representing the previous Current Price.

Where the previous Current Price has an open-ended or overlapping effective period,
establishing the implemented Price Record as the new Current Price must end the previous
record's current applicability from the applicable new effective time.

This transition must preserve the previous Price Record and its historical period of
applicability rather than rewriting the previous selling-price value.

The system must therefore be able to distinguish:

   ● the Price Record that applied before implementation;
   ● the effective transition point;
   ● the Price Record that applies after implementation.

Updating effective applicability to reflect that transition must not destroy the historical state
that existed before the implemented price became effective.

The previous Price Record must remain historically preserved.

Where implementation affects only part of an authorised Pricing Scope, Current Price must
be updated only for the Priceable Entities and pricing-dimension combinations actually
confirmed as implemented.

Where the actual implemented price differs materially from the authorised pricing value, the
system    must    preserve   that    difference   through    the applicable execution-variance
requirements     before   treating   the   implemented      value   as an ordinary authorised
implementation outcome.

A Current Price update must not silently modify:

   ● the authorised Pricing Proposal version;
   ● its submitted decision snapshot;
   ● the authorised pricing value;
   ● the historical current price used as the decision baseline.

Where implementation occurs outside Owómidé, the workspace must not represent the new
value as Current Price until implementation has been recorded or confirmed through the
applicable execution process.

The resulting Current Price must remain traceable to the implementation event that
established it.

title: Bounded External Integration
requirement:
14.28.     EXPORT-028 Bounded External Integration

The MVP must support bounded integration with selected external systems where those
integrations materially improve the ability to exchange pricing context or authorised pricing
work with the organisation's existing operating environment.

Supported integrations may include selected:

   ● spreadsheet and productivity systems;
   ● ERP platforms;
   ● commerce or marketplace platforms;
   ● other business systems required by validated MVP customers.

An integration may support inbound data exchange, outbound authorised pricing handoff or
both, according to the capabilities of the supported connector.

The MVP is not required to provide broad connector coverage, universal bidirectional
synchronisation or autonomous execution across an organisation's technology stack.

Where a native connector is unavailable, the customer must remain able to complete the
core Owómidé pricing workflow through supported manual entry, structured import, export
and operational handoff mechanisms.

Specific integrations must be prioritised according to validated customer and pilot
requirements rather than treated as universal MVP dependencies.
